glucose-6-phosphatase activity in the mammary gland is affected by parity and breed of cows, and that the activity is affected by time from last milting and stage of lactations.
glucose and G6 phosphate are present in milk and that they are indicators of physiological conditions in cows.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of metabolite biomarkers in milk as potential indicators of the energy status in mammary tissue, and the potential for use of these biomarkers for on-farm surveillance systems.
the use of free glucose, G6P, lactose, citrate and other variables as potential biomarkers of metabolic status in the mammary gland of the dairy cow.
the identification of potential biomarkers in milk that could be used as early indicators of physiological conditions in dairy cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the concentration of free glucose and glucose 6 phosphate in milk is a reflection of the physiological state of the mammary gland and can be used as biomarkers of the physiological state in dairy cows.
glucose-6-phosphatase is not active in the lactating bovine mammary epithelial cell.
free glucose and GGP are indicators of the energy status of mammary epithelial cell pre-secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucose-6-phosphatase activity is a sensitive and dynamic marker for monitoring energy status of the cow.
free glucose and GGP are indicators of specific physiological state of the cow, but not lactation stage.
free glucose and GGP can be used to monitor the metabolic health of dairy cows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucose and glucose- 6-phosphate in cow milk are indicators of the energy status in the mammary gland.
glucose and G6-P in milk reflect the energy status of mammary epithelial cell.
free glucose and GGP in milk are indicators of physiological states in the mammary gland.
